entries.proposition: One male infant carries a de novo heterozygous 16q deletion including WWOX, ANKRD11, ZNF778, CDH15 and CDH13, with callosal dysgenesis, hydrocephaly and microcephaly.

entries.proposition: Exome sequencing was limited to six selected patients.
entries.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed in six selected patients whose clinical phenotype remained incompletely explained after chromosomal microarray analysis.

entries.proposition: Only four exome-sequenced patients carried variants, listed in Table 1.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 6. The montage carries array-CGH or MLPA panels for P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P7, P9, P10, P11, P12-P13, P14, P15, P16 and P17 (legend and panel labels agree). There is NO P8 panel: the 16q23q24 deletion that includes WWOX is evidenced in the paper only by its Table 3 row (hg18 interval, inheritance, classification), not by any profile, FISH or karyotype image. The paper calls the montage representative, so the omission is not a contradiction.

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 3B (and arithmetic). The ideogram marks chromosome 16 with one red star on the long arm (pathogenic or likely pathogenic), consistent with P8's classification; it carries no breakpoints or genes. Printed yields recompute: 10 / 54 = 18.5 percent; 16 / 54 = 29.6 percent; 4 / 107 = 3.7 percent karyotype-abnormal; P8 interval 87,891,103 - 74,718,513 = 13,172,590 bp (about 13.2 Mb, derived from the printed hg18 interval; Table 3 prints no size).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3A boxes: 107 patients with CCA; karyotype n=107, 4 abnormal (3,7%); array CGH n=54, 10 CNV pathogenic/likely pathogenic (18,5%); FISH 7 cases; MLPA; WES n=6, 4 VUS. Figure 3B: red star on the long arm of chromosome 16.
